register.name: Eurobonds of the Republic of Belarus
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · coupons of USD 24.0M equivalent on Belarus-2026 and Belarus-2031, 21 and 25 August 2025 · Bank of Russia: payments and exchange in 2026
register.note: Payments credited in full to a separate account at ASB Belarusbank under Resolution No. 212/10 of 6 April 2022
register.text: The Republic’s international bonds, among them Belarus-2026 and Belarus-2031. Under Resolution No. 212/10 of the Council of Ministers and the National Bank on temporary measures for external state debt (6 April 2022), the Ministry of Finance credits payments to a separate account at ASB Belarusbank; the Bank of Russia states that in 2026 holders may receive coupons and present the bonds for redemption through Russian infrastructure, or exchange them for government securities of the Republic of Belarus.
by: Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Belarus

register.name: Rescheduling of payments on Russian state loans, 2025 agreement
register.detail: Signed in Minsk on 27 June 2025 and in Moscow on 30 June 2025 · ratified by the State Duma, January 2026 · Federal Law No. 7-FZ of 30 January 2026
register.note: The provisions of the agreement are confidential
register.text: An agreement between the Governments of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Belarus that changes the terms of certain intergovernmental agreements and provides for the rescheduling of payments by Belarus on Russian state loans. The Russian Government submitted it to the State Duma on 15 January 2026.
by: Government of the Republic of Belarus

register.name: Concessional loan for medical equipment
register.detail: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 489 of 9 September 2025 · 20-year term · to be drawn in 2025–2026
register.note: The Ministry of Finance is authorised to negotiate and sign the loan agreement within the approved draft
register.text: A concessional loan of 474.1 million Chinese yuan from the Export-Import Bank of China, for a term of 20 years, to fit Belarusian healthcare institutions with medical equipment. It serves the health standard.

register.name: Deferral of payments on Russian state loans, 2024 agreement
register.detail: Agreement signed in Moscow on 25 April 2024 · protocol of 11 July 2024 · ratification laws published 20 March 2025
register.note: About $800 million of payments deferred, according to the Deputy Finance Minister of Russia
register.text: An intergovernmental agreement and its protocol that postpone payments by Belarus on Russian government loans: principal from 1 April to 31 December 2024 and interest from 1 July to 31 December 2024, to the period 2031–2036. Russia’s ratification laws were passed by the State Duma on 4 March 2025 and the Federation Council on 14 March 2025.
by: Government of the Republic of Belarus

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Pine and birch forest in morning mist, Belarus

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Golden grain fields and birch trees under a wide sky, Belarus

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A wide avenue of neoclassical buildings in Minsk at evening, Belarus

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A winding river through reed beds and water meadows, Belarus

items.name: The Land
items.label: Land area, 2023
items.text: Territory to farm, power and protect.
items.alt: Fields, forests and blue lakes stretching to the horizon, Belarus

items.name: Eberbach-Polesye
items.text: A company in Mozyr, described by UNDP as a social commercial enterprise, that opened the first production of polyurethane tyres for wheelchairs in Belarus in 2025, so that people with disabilities can buy quality products in Belarus at a low price instead of ordering them from China. About 24,000 people in Belarus use wheelchairs; through the initiative, 150 have already received new tyres free of charge.

items.name: Raik (public association)
items.text: A Mozyr association that first opened a coffee-roasting workshop and then, with UNDP support, the first fully barrier-free space in the country for learning to make coffee, where a person in a wheelchair can train as a barista or coffee roaster.

items.name: ApiMir
items.text: A centre for the development and promotion of beekeeping in Zhlobin district, set up with the support of UNDP and the local authorities, with a demonstration apiary and training and consultations for beginning and experienced beekeepers from across Belarus on turning a traditional craft into a profitable business.

items.name: Eco-Innovation Fund
items.text: A local fund for the support of entrepreneurship and rural development in Bragin district, through which local farmers have learned to use environmentally clean technologies for growing crops, raising livestock and making cheese.
